symbols.name: digit width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each radix digit.
symbols.quote: Fix a digit width $b$, the number of bits in each radix digit.

symbols.name: digit count
symbols.meaning: The number of radix digits in each input, $\lceil n/b \rceil$.
symbols.quote: Let $m = \lceil n/b \rceil$ be the number of digits in each input.

symbols.name: first input digit
symbols.meaning: The $i$-th radix digit of the first input, an integer in $\{0,\dots,2^b-1\}$.
symbols.quote: The digit $u_i$, for $0 \le i \le m-1$, is the $i$-th radix digit of the first input, and $v_i$ is the $i$-th radix digit of the second input, each in $\{0,\dots,2^b-1\}$.

symbols.name: second input digit
symbols.meaning: The $i$-th radix digit of the second input, an integer in $\{0,\dots,2^b-1\}$.
symbols.quote: The digit $u_i$, for $0 \le i \le m-1$, is the $i$-th radix digit of the first input, and $v_i$ is the $i$-th radix digit of the second input, each in $\{0,\dots,2^b-1\}$.

symbols.name: formal variable
symbols.meaning: A formal variable whose powers mark the coefficient positions of the digit polynomials.
symbols.quote: Let $t$ be a formal variable marking coefficient positions.

symbols.name: first digit polynomial
symbols.meaning: The polynomial $U(t)$ whose coefficients are the digits of the first input.
symbols.quote: The polynomial $U(t)$ has the digits of the first input as coefficients, and $V(t)$ has those of the second

symbols.name: second digit polynomial
symbols.meaning: The polynomial $V(t)$ whose coefficients are the digits of the second input.
symbols.quote: The polynomial $U(t)$ has the digits of the first input as coefficients, and $V(t)$ has those of the second

symbols.name: product polynomial
symbols.meaning: The product $U(t)V(t)$, whose value at $t = 2^b$ is the integer product of the inputs.
symbols.quote: Let $W(t) = U(t)V(t)$ be the product polynomial.

symbols.name: product coefficient
symbols.meaning: The $k$-th coefficient of $W$, the sum of $u_i v_j$ over $i+j=k$.
symbols.quote: Its $k$-th coefficient $w_k$ is the sum of $u_i v_j$ over $i+j=k$, a convolution of the two digit lists.

relations.quote: Computing $W$ from the digit lists is a [Cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) of length at least $2m-1$, so the integer product is reduced to a cyclic convolution.
